The Q&A session video from one of Apple's most iconic events of the past 20 years has been circulating online — watch it before it gets taken down. Here's the video.

Watch it before Apple removes it

Even if you weren't closely following Apple in 2010, you've probably heard about "Antennagate," and the press conference that forced Steve Jobs to cut short his family vacation in Hawaii to fly back.

If you're not familiar with the story, here's the background: shortly after the iPhone 4 went on sale, users discovered that signal strength dropped dramatically depending on how you held the phone.

The backlash was so intense that Apple was forced to hold an emergency event just weeks after the iPhone 4 launched.

At the event, Jobs explained that signal attenuation wasn't a problem unique to the iPhone 4, and offered users a free case to prevent their palm from touching the antenna directly, or a full refund.

After the event concluded, Jobs appeared alongside then-COO Tim Cook and Apple's Senior Vice President of Mac Hardware Engineering Bob Mansfield for a Q&A session with reporters.

Since then, there have been various accounts of what happened that day, including John Gruber recalling how he posed a question that forced Jobs, Cook, and Mansfield to pull un-cased iPhones from their pockets, producing one of the iconic photos of that era. But actual video of the session had never surfaced. Until today.

Earlier this week, the YouTube channel Sir Mix-A-Lot Rare Music (which appears to have no connection to the actual Sir Mix-A-Lot) uploaded the full 47-minute Q&A session, available below:

It's unclear how the channel obtained the footage, or whether Apple will issue a takedown. But now that it's out, even if the original is removed, copies will easily spread again.

The fact that the video hasn't been taken down yet is itself a good sign. Still, if you want to witness this piece of Apple history firsthand, be sure to watch it soon.

Were you following Apple during the Antennagate era? Share your memories in the comments.
